sync: v1.0.3 — 中文名 AI 钥匙；套件二改名生意操盘手

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

llm.summary: This skill is a disclosed router for the AI KEY skill family, with local discovery and memory behavior that fits its stated purpose.

dimensions.detail: The skill asks the agent to read local config, vault references, selected downstream skill docs, and installed aikey skill metadata; this is proportionate for a local router, but users should expect local path and skill-environment discovery.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: No package installation, remote code retrieval, dependency installation, or hidden install-time behavior was found. The included shell script is a local read-only discovery helper.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Triggers include broad casual phrases, which may activate it when the user did not explicitly type /aikey, but the runtime instructions mostly constrain it to routing, prompt generation, or a short onboarding demo.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The wider aikey family documents writing outputs and validated lessons into configured directories or memory. This persistence is disclosed and purpose-aligned, with no hidden service, backdoor, or destructive persistence found.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The skill presents itself as an entry point for routing content and business tasks, onboarding users, and suggesting next steps; the inspected instructions are consistent with that purpose.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install this if you want an AI KEY family router and are comfortable with it reading local aikey skill metadata, selected skill docs, configured project/vault files, and writing workflow outputs or lessons in configured locations. Review the memory/writeback behavior if you will use it with sensitive business, account, or personal examples.
llm.findings:
[TP4] expected: The local skill enumeration script is real, but it is limited to aikey-prefixed skill directories, reads descriptions, and prints paths for routing; this is a privacy note rather than evidence of malicious tool poisoning.
[AE1] expected: The instruction to fully read a selected downstream skill is part of progressive routing into another installed skill, not an apparent attempt to evade review of this artifact.
[SQP-1] expected: The broad trigger phrases increase accidental activation risk, but they are disclosed in the manifest and fit the skill's role as a public entry point for unsure users.
[SDI-1] expected: The output and memory persistence language is disclosed as part of the aikey workflow and is scoped to configured project directories or skill memory rather than hidden system persistence.
[SDI-1] expected: The shell-based dynamic discovery path is purpose-aligned with choosing among actually installed aikey skills; the script is read-only and does not execute discovered skill code.
[SDI-4] expected: The onboarding no-write promise appears specific to the short demo mode, while other modes and downstream skills may write outputs or memory; this should be clearer but is not deceptive exfiltration or destructive behavior.
